info.title: Qwen Managed Agent Public and WebShell API
info.description: Canonical contract for the public Managed Agent resources and the WebShell adapter. partial means that the route exists but generated types and full contract tests are pending; planned means that the route or field is not implemented. Workspace context and cwd operations are v1.9 target contracts, not current server capabilities. v1.10 adds planned command admission, Actions, lifecycle and actor authorization. v1.12 refines planned W0 creation discovery, actor-specific create hints and explicit default selection. Filter planned fields as well as routes from production SDKs. v1.13 moves this contract into the Qwen Code repository as its single source and records the shipped rename, archive, unarchive and delete routes as partial. v1.14 integrates W0d workspace discovery, the WebShell workspace lookup, and empty-session binding as partial; workspace_binding/workspaceBinding advertises this narrow flow without enabling workspace execution or context switching. v1.15 adds the archived, archiving and deleting Session statuses and the cancelling Turn status, requires request_id in error envelopes, declares the error responses that the server returns, and marks Session create, list and get on both surfaces implemented. v1.16 adds the planned Stage H task contract (SessionTaskView as PublicTask, task list, detail, events and cancel) and names the MCP catalog, hook catalog, automation and channel resources as planned; their shapes arrive with Stages H1 to H6. v1.17 implements event replay: events carry their schema and projection versions and a top-level Item and Part identity, JSON event pages return has_more and next_cursor and accept limits up to 1000, and a persisted replay floor answers expired cursors with 409 cursor_expired in JSON and one agent.session.resync_required frame over SSE; it marks the public event query and stream, the WebShell event stream and the WebShell transcript implemented. v1.18 implements the durable Session lifecycle (Stage D4): close, archive and delete answer 202 with a command operation on both surfaces, an archive requires a closed Session, a deleted Session leaves a tombstone whose operations stay readable, and the operation query serves them; unarchive restores a closed Session, and Session capabilities advertise session_lifecycle. v1.19 serves the task list and detail on both surfaces as partial (Stage H0c): the Session store projects them from the Stage H records the Session authority commits, a task.updated Session event announces each change of a task's view, and Session capabilities advertise tasks. Task events and cancel stay planned until a slice's tasks produce output and accept a cancel. v1.20 implements the Turn read model (Stage D5): the public Turn list and detail read a Session's Turns without their input, newest first by creation time in milliseconds and then Turn ID, with an opaque cursor; a deleted Session's Turns are not readable, and the durable admission fields of a Turn stay planned until D7. v1.21 declares on the task list, detail and event routes of both surfaces the 403 actor_scope_mismatch that the tenant filter answers on every /v1/agents/ and WebShell route, as the Session and Turn reads already do, and the shared Forbidden response names it; a caller that cannot read a task still gets 404. v1.22 adds deployment-opted-in creation with an initial Workspace file-tool Turn (G0) on the public and WebShell surfaces; the fixed server-owned profile does not enable later Workspace operations. v1.23 settles the planned task event and cancel semantics: a durable retention floor, committed-prefix publication, stable cursors, Artifact visibility before expiry, bounded backlog under archival failure, ordered idempotent cancellation and command outcomes. Clients tolerate unknown optional event fields across minor versions. Task events and cancel remain planned. v1.24 serves the read-only Session MCP catalog as partial (Stage H1), projecting display metadata and schemas from committed records without Runtime identities, credentials or production profile enablement. v1.25 implements permission Actions (Stage D6b) on both surfaces: list, get and respond, projected from the Session's action.changed records; a WebShell permission Action carries inputRevision, policyRevision, functionCallId, toolName and expiresAt, its option ids allow and deny are stable, a Turn has at most one requested approval at a time, and a response is a durable command operation carrying requestId. v1.26 declares the tenant filter's 403 actor_scope_mismatch on every covered public and WebShell route, including planned routes, and pins the refusal code in contract traffic. v1.27 adds O3 durable tool-result projection, artifact metadata, immutable range/streaming content and WebShell result reads. Artifact capability requires a configured O3 reader and a Workspace-bound Session; execution admission remains independent. v1.28 admits later Turns of a Workspace-bound Session for the Session's creator under the deployment's Workspace files opt-in, including cancel and rename; WebShell Session capabilities advertise the per-caller workspaceTurns flag. v1.29 implements the AgentDefinition routes (Stage D8a): create, get and update store tenant-scoped, immutable revisions with a content digest, and an unchanged update adds no revision. Sessions still pin qwen-code and the configured revision, and no definition field changes execution yet.

post.description: Stores revision 1 of a new tenant-scoped definition under a server-generated agent ID. The same Idempotency-Key with the same body replays the original revision; a different body answers 409 idempotency_conflict. Sessions do not use definitions yet, and no field changes execution.

get.description: Reads the latest revision, or the one named by revision. An unknown agent ID or revision answers 404 agent_not_found.

200.description: Requested or current agent revision.

post.description: Stores the next immutable revision. Content whose digest equals the latest revision stores nothing and answers with that revision. The same Idempotency-Key and request replay the recorded revision. If another update takes the same next revision number, the losing write answers 409 agent_revision_conflict without recording its key, so that key can be retried. The returned revision may be superseded by a concurrent update before the response arrives.

202.description: The next immutable revision, or the latest revision unchanged when the submitted content digest already equals it; no revision is appended in that case.

post.description: Workspace selection is persisted with the original actor-scoped creation receipt. With the deployment's G0 file admission opt-in, qwen-code Sessions in an authorized, preregistered Workspace may include initial input under the fixed preapproved file-tool profile. Public callers cannot select the profile. Otherwise Workspace creation must have empty input. The Session creator may submit later Turns and cancel its running Turns under the same opt-in, and may rename the Session, while the creator currently holds Workspace read and create grants on a registry row whose state is ACTIVE and the Session is an active, undeleted qwen-code Session on the frozen execution profile; Workspace close follows its separate close capability and lifecycle admission; archive, delete and unarchive follow their separate retention capabilities after reliable Workspace close; cwd operations remain gated. This surface has no per-caller capability flag for later Turns, so callers must handle 409 workspace_unavailable. Check replay before resolving defaults; a durable binding is not proof of Runtime readiness.

202.description: Session accepted after durable command admission.

200.description: Sessions ordered by updated_at and id descending.
Session state.

patch.description: Renames the Session. Shipped before the v1.10 lifecycle review, which does not cover it.

200.description: Renamed Session.

delete.description: Unbound Sessions accept active, closed or archived state. Returns 409 turn_active while a Turn is active and session_operation_active while another lifecycle change is pending. The same key from the same actor returns the original operation, also after the Session was deleted. Workspace-bound delete accepts only closed or archived Sessions with completed reliable-close evidence and the creator with current read access. Active deletion returns 409 session_state_conflict. Completion atomically retires private recovery/publication access with the tombstone, operation receipt and terminal event; it calls neither Harness nor Runtime and erases no shared Workspace files or backup bytes. Operations remain readable under current read grants; the same authorized actor/key can replay after deletion. A readable non-creator returns 403; missing close evidence returns 409 workspace_unavailable.

202.description: Deletion accepted. The Session stops accepting input and reads deleting. If it was active, the operation first closes it as a close does; it then drains the Session's Runtime binding and leaves a tombstone: Session reads return 404, while its operations stay readable. The shared Workspace is never deleted, and no Session content is erased yet. 202 does not mean that tools have stopped.

get.description: Returns JSON by default. Accept text/event-stream or stream=true to receive SSE. Last-Event-ID takes precedence over after. A cursor below replay_floor_sequence gets 409 cursor_expired as JSON; a stream instead sends one agent.session.resync_required frame and closes.

200.description: Event page or SSE stream.

schema.description: SSE frames whose id is the public sequence and whose data is a PublicEvent. An expired cursor ends the stream with one agent.session.resync_required frame that has no id; x-qwen-resync-frame is its data.

get.description: Turns of this Session, newest first: by creation time in milliseconds, which created_at shows in whole seconds, then by id, both descending. next_cursor names the last Turn of the page and is null on the last page; a page never repeats or skips a Turn that existed when the first page was read. 400 invalid_limit for a 32-bit integer limit outside 1 to 100, invalid_request for a limit that is not a 32-bit integer, and invalid_cursor for a cursor that does not decode to the createdAt:turnId form this server issues. 404 session_not_found for an unknown, deleted or unreadable Session.

200.description: Turn page.

get.description: 404 session_not_found for an unknown, deleted or unreadable Session, and turn_not_found for a Turn that this Session does not have; an id that differs from a Turn's only by trailing spaces does not find it. 400 invalid_request for a Turn id longer than 64 characters.

200.description: Turn state.
Materialized items and snapshot watermark.
Authorized artifact metadata page.

get.description: Authorized artifacts, newest first by creation sequence and then artifact ID. Opaque cursors are bound to tenant, Session and the first page watermark; pages do not repeat or skip retained artifacts present at that watermark. next_cursor names the last artifact and is null on the last page. 400 invalid_limit rejects limits outside 1..100; 400 invalid_cursor rejects malformed cursors or cursors from another tenant or Session. Discard an invalid cursor and restart from the first page.

200.description: Exact immutable bytes; streamed with bounded memory.

206.description: Exact immutable bytes; streamed with bounded memory.

410.description: Reserved for future retention support; O3 does not expire retained representations.

get.description: Requires a trusted actor and current Workspace read/raw-content grants. revision is mandatory. One range up to 1 MiB; malformed, multiple, or oversized ranges return 400. A mismatched If-Range selects the full response. Authorization precedes validators and range parsing. No latest-version fallback or transparent compression.

200.description: WebShell session page.
WebShell session.
Event transcript page.

post.description: Without a cursor, a Session that has a Snapshot returns all of its Items, the events up to the Snapshot other than turn.accepted, item.output_text.delta, item.reasoning.delta, item.tool_call.updated and item.tool_result.updated, which the Items already hold, and every event after it. Otherwise, and for an olderCursor, limit bounds the page of events.

POST SSE consumed through fetch response.body. An afterSequence below the replay floor ends the stream with one agent.session.resync_required frame instead of a 409; reload the transcript and resume after its lastSequence.

200.description: SSE stream.

schema.description: SSE frames whose id is the public sequence and whose data is a WebShellEvent. The agent.session.resync_required frame has no id; x-qwen-resync-frame is its data.

post.description: Maps workspaceId/cwdRelative to public Workspace selection without using environmentId or absolute cwd. Shares G0's opt-in initial file-tool Turn admission and fixed server-owned profile with public Session creation. The Session creator may submit later Turns and cancel its running Turns under the same opt-in, and may rename the Session, while the creator currently holds Workspace read and create grants on a registry row whose state is ACTIVE and the Session is an active, undeleted qwen-code Session on the frozen execution profile; Workspace close follows its separate close capability and lifecycle admission; archive, delete and unarchive follow their separate retention capabilities after reliable Workspace close; cwd operations remain gated. The per-caller workspaceTurns capability on this surface advertises the same rule. Freeze selection with the original idempotency key; admission does not prove physical directory readiness.

get.description: Only readable preregistered workspaces, ordered by stable workspace id. Opaque cursors are bound to tenant, actor and filters; ACLs are rechecked on each page. Return actor-specific creation hints, pre-Session capability discovery and the authorized explicit default even when it is outside this page. No physical paths are exposed and no Runtime is started.

200.description: Authorized durable resource view; no Runtime startup required.
Authorized durable resource view; no Runtime startup required.

post.description: W2: same-workspace only. Replay the original operation before revision/busy checks. Reject active or queued input and context holds. Poll the operation or await session.context.changed; do not treat 202 as activation.

get.description: Reads one operation of the Session. Close, archive and delete operations are served now; cwd, command and task operations arrive with their slices. 404 operation_not_found for an unknown operation.

200.description: Authorized operation with its latest durable status, readable without Runtime startup and after the Session was deleted. Reading is not a replay, so replayed is false.

Accepts an active Session; 409 session_state_conflict otherwise. Supported hosted-workspace-files/1 Sessions may close when session_close is true. Only the creator with current read access may close a bound Session: unreadable returns 404, readable non-creator returns 403. Active, cancelling or approval-waiting Turns return 409 turn_active; another pending lifecycle operation returns session_operation_active. Unsupported Workspace close returns workspace_unavailable. The same actor and key replay the original operation.

202.description: Close durably accepted. The Session stops accepting input and reads closing. A bound Session completes only after its permanent Runtime admission fence is stored, no valid journal writer or unsettled execution remains, all original Runtime Sessions and holders are released, and original worker stop proof is persisted; the Session then reads closed. Unknown original identities or executions report recovery_blocked with a stable failure_code and keep the Session closing. History, Artifacts and Workspace files are retained. 202 does not mean that tools have stopped.

post.description: Accepts a closed Session; 409 session_state_conflict otherwise, session_operation_active while another lifecycle change is pending. Workspace-bound archive requires a closed Session with completed reliable-close evidence and the creator with current read access. It completes atomically during admission, preserves data and the permanent close fence, and calls neither Harness nor Runtime. A readable non-creator returns 403; missing close evidence returns 409 workspace_unavailable.

202.description: Archive requires a closed Session and retains history. Java is its only authority, so a new archive is complete when it is admitted.

post.description: Synchronously restores an archived Session to closed. Workspace-bound Sessions require completed reliable-close evidence and the creator with current read access (404 unreadable, 403 readable non-creator). Bound keys are tenant/Session/actor scoped. Replay returns the current visible Session without repeating the mutation; a deleted Session returns 404. The permanent close fence is preserved and no Harness or Runtime call is made.

Read one authorized Workspace by its logical ID; absent or unreadable Workspaces return 404. No Runtime is started.

200.description: Authorized durable resource view; no Runtime startup required.

Tasks of this Session, newest first (created_at descending, then id descending), merged from the record domains the server projects — Monitor runs today, the others arrive with their stages. Settled tasks stay listed. The projection is rebuilt from durable domain records, so task IDs and order survive a restart. A task.updated Session event, with data.taskId and data.state, announces each change of a task's view.
Current task view, including settled tasks. 404 task_not_found covers tasks outside the caller scope.

Task events strictly after the cursor, oldest first, published as a committed prefix per task: no event may become visible at or before any previously returned event, page or output_cursor position. 400 invalid_event_cursor rejects a malformed cursor or one from another task. The durable retention floor is the position after the newest expired event, initially the stream start; only an oldest prefix expires. 409 cursor_expired means strictly below that floor, even when no events remain; equality is valid. Its replay_floor_sequence and snapshot_through_sequence stay absent because task cursors are opaque. Cursor identity, logical position, payload and accepted schema/projection versions survive rebuilds, restarts and archival; retention may still expire a cursor. Any output-producing task requires capabilities.artifacts. An output event holds back its own expiry and every later event until its full text is durably readable in an Artifact and discoverable by subsequent recovery reads, including through a potentially lagging task projection. Time retention is a target under healthy archival, not an unconditional deletion deadline. Archival failure pins the floor; H3 must bound durable backlog and apply producer backpressure and admission blocking before capacity is exhausted, or leave output-producing tasks disabled. Never silently discard accepted output. After cursor_expired, read one event page from the floor without after and save next_cursor; do not wait for has_more=false because an active producer may never catch up. Then read a fresh task view and discover/read its Artifacts, then resume from the saved page cursor, including events held back by the first page limit, not the new view's output_cursor. If the floor overtakes the reader, restart recovery; never treat another 409 as an empty page. Until older Artifacts can be enumerated and attributed to the task, H3 must prevent rotation beyond the 100 artifact_refs entries; afterward recovery must also enumerate older Artifacts. Recovery is guaranteed while the task and its Artifacts remain readable under their retention and authorization rules. Stage H3 defines stable output segments for joining Artifacts and events without overlap. 400 unsupported_feature when the Session does not serve tasks (capabilities.tasks is false).

202.description: Java durably accepted the cancellation and owns delivery; 202 does not prove owner acceptance or physical stop. After the tenant/actor filter and request decoding, validate Idempotency-Key (missing: 400 invalid_request; malformed: 400 invalid_idempotency_key), then current access (404 for an unreadable Session/task, then 403 task_forbidden for a readable task the actor may not cancel), then idempotent replay. The domain is tenant/session/operation-kind/actor/key; the digest includes task_id and excludes trace-only request IDs. While the record is retained and access remains valid, the same key and digest returns the same operation with its latest durable state and replayed=true; another digest returns 409 idempotency_conflict. Only new requests check capabilities.tasks (400 unsupported_feature), then Session active state (409 session_not_active otherwise, including closing, closed, archived and deleting), then action_capabilities containing cancel (409 task_action_unavailable otherwise). Admission requires no other open operation on the Session: cancel operations share the durable operation table with the lifecycle commands, which admit one open operation per Session, so any open operation answers 409 session_operation_active and an open cancel blocks close, archive and delete the same way. Atomically recheck admission and create the operation, serializing with Session/task transitions; a concurrent same-key winner replays before new-request state checks. Different keys that each pass admission create different operations, although physical stop requests may be coalesced or repeated safely; each operation gets its own recorded outcome. completed means the task authority durably recorded cancellation and returned a receipt; failed proves it was not accepted and will not be delivered again, with failure_code; recovery_blocked means acceptance is unknown and requires reconciliation before any re-execution. Retryable delivery failures remain pending/running. task_cancel never has status cancelled because cancellation commands cannot be withdrawn. Only physical cancellation settlement makes the task cancelled; a natural terminal outcome is preserved and an unknown physical outcome makes the task recovery_blocked independently of operation acceptance. Capability or state changes do not invalidate replay, but missing/deleted resources or revoked access may still return 404/403.

200.description: Same authorized task semantics as the public API.
Same authorized task semantics as the public API.

Same authorized task semantics as the public task events route, including the durable retention floor, committed-prefix publication, Artifact recovery order and client tolerance of unknown optional fields and event types.

202.description: Same authorized task cancellation semantics as the public API: key validation, current access, idempotent replay, then new-request capability, Session and task checks. Replay returns the same operation and latest durable state. 202 is durable admission, completed is authority acceptance, and neither proves physical stop. Admission requires no other open operation on the Session (409 session_operation_active), as on the lifecycle routes.

200.description: Sanitized tools, resources and prompts from the latest published catalog of each server in this Session. A failed or pending replacement preserves the previous published catalog. Released or unpublished catalogs are stale. This read-only projection does not enable a production MCP profile or accept server configuration.

Sanitized planning summary of the latest settled Hook registration in this Session. A pending or failed replacement preserves the previous catalog. Hook recipes, prompts, credentials and handler implementations are never returned.
Planned name only: channel connections and routes; chat input still uses the Session event API. Stage H5 defines the response.
Planned name only: outbound deliveries of a channel with per-segment receipts. Stage H5 defines the response.
Planned name only: automation definitions; definitions and run history page separately. Stage H6 defines the response.

Workspace-bound Sessions require completed reliable-close evidence and the creator with current read access (404 unreadable, 403 readable non-creator). Bound keys are tenant/Session/actor scoped. trustedTenant.name: X-Qwen-Tenant-Id
trustedTenant.description: Injected by the trusted authenticated gateway, never trusted from browser input.

trustedActor.name: X-Qwen-Actor-Id
trustedActor.description: Verified actor injected by the authenticated gateway together with tenant; browser-supplied headers are stripped. Resource ACLs and Action responder eligibility are mandatory. This header is not a browser credential.

TaskEventCursor.name: after
TaskEventCursor.description: Opaque task event cursor: an event cursor, a page next_cursor or a task output_cursor. Omit it to read from the durable retention floor. Strictly below the floor is 409 cursor_expired; equality is valid, including with no retained events.

IdempotentReplay.description: True when an accepted command or operation was replayed for the same idempotency key and digest without repeating its mutation. Session mutation responses represent the current visible Session; operation responses represent the original operation at its current state.

RequestId.description: Trace-only correlation identifier; never an idempotency key.

Forbidden.description: The authenticated actor belongs to another tenant than X-Qwen-Tenant-Id or has an invalid ID (actor_scope_mismatch, which the tenant filter answers on every /v1/agents/ and WebShell route), or the resource is readable but the actor lacks this operation or the original Action responder permission. Artifact content reads may also return artifact_content_forbidden when the actor cannot read the original bytes.

Unauthorized.description: A trusted actor is required for this request but none was supplied.

NotFound.description: Resource absent or outside the caller tenant scope.

CursorExpired.description: Replay cursor is older than the retained replay floor.

TaskCursorExpired.description: Task event cursor is strictly below the task's durable retention floor, which survives an empty retained set; equality is valid. The envelope's replay_floor_sequence and snapshot_through_sequence stay absent because task cursors are opaque.

Unavailable.description: A dependency such as the Hosted Harness is unavailable; retry later.

catalog_revision.description: The pinned catalog revision; null while no catalog has been published.

agent_revision.description: Optional explicit revision; omitted resolves current revision atomically at admission.

stream.description: Phase one requires false; stream through the events route.

workspace.description: W0. Only omission allows default resolution; null or an empty object is invalid. Resolve and persist an explicit authorized tenant default on first admission; no default means workspace_required. The caller request digest retains an omission marker; replay resolves the original receipt before defaults. A changed default must never rebind a retry. Unavailable W0 support rejects rather than ignores this field.

CommandAdmission.description: With durable_operations enabled, all three target fields are returned. accepted means Java durable delivery responsibility, not model execution. Missing fields retain the deployed legacy response semantics.

creation_operation_id.description: Original create_session operation; creation retries resolve this identity before allocating another Session.

replay_floor_sequence.description: Events at or below this sequence may be pruned. A replay cursor below it has expired.

workspace.description: Absent for unbound legacy records, whose execution stays blocked pending evidence-based migration. Ready means committed context, not an active Runtime gate.

session_lifecycle.description: True when the Session accepts close, archive and delete operations; false for a Workspace-bound Session.

session_close.description: Deployment support for close independently of archive/delete; bound files Sessions require durable worker stop support. This is not actor authorization: admission also requires creator ownership and current read access.

session_archive.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

session_unarchive.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

session_delete.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

PublicEvent.description: A committed event, replayed with the versions and identity it was accepted with. A stream.reconciled event is the exception: it means that Harness recovery retracted earlier deltas of its Turn, which now have empty text and no item_id or content_part_id, and that later deltas may name other Parts. Reload the Items until the snapshot_through_sequence they return reaches the sequence of the stream.reconciled event, then resume after that snapshot_through_sequence, not after the stream.reconciled event; the Snapshot is rebuilt meanwhile.

SessionResyncRequired.description: Data of the agent.session.resync_required SSE frame. Read the Session and its Items, then resume after the snapshot_through_sequence that the Items list returns; the value in this frame can be older.

created_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, Turn, Event and Item resources report.

skills.description: null is the same as omitting the field.

mcp_servers.description: null is the same as omitting the field.

metadata.description: null is the same as omitting the field.

next_cursor.description: The after value for the next page; null when has_more is false.

environmentId.description: Planned; phase one rejects non-blank values.

WebShellAdmission.description: With durable_operations enabled, all three target fields are returned. accepted means Java durable delivery responsibility, not model execution. Missing fields retain the deployed legacy response semantics.

creationOperationId.description: Original create_session operation; creation retries resolve this identity before allocating another Session.

workspaceTurns.description: True when the caller may submit later Turns of this Workspace-bound Session, cancel its running Turns and rename it: the deployment enables Workspace files, the caller created the Session and currently holds Workspace read and create grants on a registry row whose state is ACTIVE, and the Session is an active qwen-code Session on the frozen execution profile. False for every other caller and for unbound Sessions, which do not use it.

sessionClose.description: Deployment support for close independently of archive/delete. Admission also requires creator ownership and current read access for a bound Session.

sessionArchive.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

sessionUnarchive.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

sessionDelete.description: Optional support for this retention operation. For a Workspace-bound Session requires completed reliable-close evidence; authorization and source-state validation still apply.

WebShellEvent.description: A committed event, replayed with the versions and identity it was accepted with. A stream.reconciled event is the exception: it means that Harness recovery retracted earlier deltas of its Turn, which now have empty text and no itemId or contentPartId, and that later deltas may name other Parts. Reload the transcript and resume after its lastSequence.

WebShellResyncRequired.description: Data of the agent.session.resync_required SSE frame. Reload the transcript, then resume after its lastSequence.

WorkspaceRelativePath.description: Logical directory relative to the authorized workspace root; dot denotes root. Use slash separators. Reject absolute paths, drive prefixes, backslashes, NUL and parent segments. Runtime must verify directory existence, realpath containment and symlink safety before activation; schema validation alone is insufficient. Preserve spaces and case, normalize repeated separators and dot segments, and never percent-decode JSON values.

can_create_session.description: Current actor permission hint only; creation rechecks ACL, state and Agent/config compatibility.

workspace_context.description: True only after W0 creation, binding and private installation contracts are supported end to end.

workspace_binding.description: Supports authorized Workspace discovery, Session creation, and saved binding read-back. This capability does not advertise execution readiness. Deployments may separately opt in to an initial Workspace Read/Write/Edit Turn at creation; the Session creator may submit and cancel later Turns under the same opt-in, while close follows its separate capability and lifecycle admission; archive, delete and unarchive follow their separate retention capabilities after reliable Workspace close.

default_workspace.description: Explicit tenant default only when active and creatable by this actor; otherwise null. Included independently of the current page. A non-null default has can_create_session=true; creation revalidates it.

PublicCwdOperation.description: A completed operation returns the committed target revision. A replay returns the same operation identity and latest durable status, with replayed=true; polling itself is not replay.

canCreateSession.description: Current actor permission hint only; creation rechecks ACL, state and Agent/config compatibility.

workspaceContext.description: Same end-to-end W0 readiness as public workspace_context; missing means unsupported.

defaultWorkspace.description: Same authorized explicit default as default_workspace, including when outside this page; null if absent or not creatable. A non-null default is active and has canCreateSession=true.

WebShellCwdOperation.description: A completed operation returns the committed target revision. A replay returns the same operation identity and latest durable status, with replayed=true; polling itself is not replay.

PermissionAction.description: At most one requested Hosted approval per Turn. allow and deny are stable option IDs. Tool arguments are read from Items by function_call_id (functionCallId in WebShell). Public timestamps are milliseconds, as recorded by the Harness. Decision receipts are opaque product IDs.

ActionResponseRequest.description: Validate IDs, required answers, selection cardinality, text eligibility and current responder permission against the original Action. Unknown/expired/cancelled/conflicting revisions cannot grant execution.

outcome.description: D6 supports decided only; vote_recorded is planned.

task_id.description: Task that a task_cancel operation targets.

failure_code.description: Reason a durable response or task cancellation failed. Action response failures come from the original committed Action, or a definitive invalid response. Workspace close recovery_blocked reports original resource identity or unsettled execution; the Session remains closing.

PublicCommandOperation.description: Receipt IDs are opaque authorized product handles, not private journal or storage refs. Input/cancel completion is command acceptance, not Turn completion or physical stop. Action completion may only record one vote. Lifecycle completion requires its cleanup facts; archive may remain java_durable because Java is its authority. Task cancel 202 is Java durable admission; completion means the authority durably recorded cancellation and returned a receipt, not that the task stopped. Task cancel failed proves non-acceptance and no further delivery, with a failure code; recovery_blocked means acceptance is unknown and needs reconciliation before re-execution. Its status is never cancelled. Physical settlement and an unknown physical outcome belong to the task, independently of operation acceptance. A completed task cancel carries admission stage harness_confirmed and delivery state confirmed with the authority's receipt; failed and recovery_blocked carry java_durable and blocked, so they are never delivered again without reconciliation.

TaskState.description: Logical run state. completed, failed and cancelled are terminal and are set only after the physical execution has settled. degraded means that the task still runs with reduced guarantees, such as a Monitor that lost its observation source. recovery_blocked means that recovery cannot prove the physical outcome: it is not settled, is never reported as success and is never re-run automatically.

TaskRuntimeState.description: Redacted state of the Runtime that hosts the task, without binding identity or generation.

TaskActionCapability.description: Actions the task supports now, the same for every caller. cancel: the cancel route accepts a new command for this task; whether a caller may use it is an authorization check (403 on the cancel route). send_input: reserved for a later capability route. read_output: the task events route returns output events for this task to any caller that can read it. read_output does not change during the task's life, and a task without it produces no output events: its output goes only to Artifacts, so the events route never filters out events that exist.

definition_revision.description: Immutable definition revision this run is pinned to, when the kind has a definition.

created_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, turn, event and item resources report.

started_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, turn, event and item resources report.

settled_at.description: Unix epoch milliseconds, unlike the seconds that the public Session, turn, event and item resources report.

output_cursor.description: Stable task event cursor after the committed tail at view read time. No event can later appear at or before it. Pass it as after to follow only new events; recovery must instead keep its saved event page cursor so it does not skip intervening output. Normal retention may expire it.

artifact_refs.description: The newest Artifacts that hold durable task output, at most 100, oldest first. Entries must not rotate out until older Artifacts can be enumerated and attributed to the task: an evicted Artifact stays readable by id through the Session artifact routes but is no longer discoverable from the task.

PublicTask.description: Read-only projection of one asynchronous task of a Session (SessionTaskView). It is rebuilt from the Session's durable domain records and is never their source of truth. It never carries a Runtime binding ID, generation, Runtime endpoint, Pod, absolute path, raw PID, SecretHandle or local sidecar; diagnostics are authorized Artifact references.

cursor.description: Stable opaque position after this event and its identity. Atomically apply the event and save this cursor to avoid duplicate application after a crash. It is never reassigned; normal retention can expire it.

truncated.description: True when the chunk was cut to the event limit; its full output is already durably readable and discoverable in the task Artifacts when the event is published.

PublicTaskEvent.description: One task event: a logical state change, a bounded output chunk, or an Artifact reference. High-volume output goes to Artifacts or bounded chunks in this paged stream, never one Session event per raw line. The closed schema validates the server's own version; clients ignore unknown optional fields and unknown types and checkpoint their cursors. Strict response validation against an older minor version is not supported. Event identity, position, payload and accepted schema/projection versions are immutable across restart, projection rebuild and archival.

definitionRevision.description: Immutable definition revision this run is pinned to, when the kind has a definition.

nextCursor.description: The last returned event cursor, never passing an event held back by limit. On an empty page, the requested position, or the durable retention floor if after was omitted. Required and never null, including when no events remain. No event may later become visible at or before this position.

after.description: Opaque task event cursor: an event cursor, a page nextCursor or a task outputCursor. Omit it to read from the durable retention floor. Strictly below the floor is 409 cursor_expired; equality is valid, including with no retained events.

TaskEventType.description: state_changed, output or artifact. The set is open: a later minor version may add types and optional fields. Clients ignore unknown optional fields and unknown types, while still checkpointing event cursors; strict validation against an older minor response schema is not supported. Existing fields forbidden for a known type cannot be repurposed on that type.

next_cursor.description: The last returned event cursor, never passing an event held back by limit. On an empty page, the requested position, or the durable retention floor if after was omitted. Required and never null, including when no events remain. No event may later become visible at or before this position.

projection_revision.description: This implementation projects each result once at revision 1. Monotonic consumers reject duplicate or stale replay events; reprojection requires a separately reviewed migration and producer.

delivery_status.description: O3 emits committed or blocked from the durable receipt. Pending is reserved for future producers and is not emitted by this implementation.
